items.title: Passengers from hantavirus ship transferred to Australian quarantine
items.description: A flight carrying five Australians and one New Zealander who were on board the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship has landed in an air force base in Perth.

items.title: Coalition tax plan could cost more than suggested in first few years
items.description: The Coalition's plan to index tax brackets could cost $35 billion in the first four years, more than has been suggested, and $44 billion in one year alone in 2035-36.

items.title: Universities warn against Coalition plan to cut foreign student numbers
items.description: Universities are bracing for foreign student numbers to absorb the bulk of cuts under a Coalition migration plan, with experts warning skilled visas would be difficult to cull.

items.title: Australia records first reported death from diphtheria in almost a decade
items.description: The Northern Territory has recorded the country's first reported death from diphtheria in almost a decade, as experts urge people to get vaccinated.

items.title: ABC boss Hugh Marks flags TV cuts as broadcaster pivots to new platforms
items.description: The ABC's managing director says the public broadcaster's biggest challenge is "stopping things" as he seeks to grow audiences on new platforms without increasing staff.

items.title: Why millennials and gen Z feel ripped off by this budget
items.description: The prime minister says this budget is about fixing intergenerational inequality, but online, gen Z and the millennials are hearing a different narrative.

items.title: Xi made a historical reference to give Trump a warning. What did it mean?
items.description: The US and China have been rivals for almost 80 years, but when the countries' leaders met in Beijing on Thursday, Xi Jinping made reference to a far more ancient feud.

items.title: Live: 'We want the straits open': Trump says China agrees on ending the Iran war
items.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping praised the building of a "stable relationship" with the US as the two world leaders met for their second day of talks. Follow live.

items.title: How likely is Delta Goodrem to bring home the Eurovision crown?
items.description: In a dazzling show of light and a powerful, pitch-perfect performance, Delta Goodrem may have just given Australia a real shot at winning Eurovision for the first time.

items.title: Ruling upheld after transgender woman excluded from female-only app
items.description: ​A landmark Federal Court ruling that the exclusion of a transgender woman from a female-only app constituted unlawful gender identity discrimination is upheld on appeal.

items.title: Israeli nationalists chant anti-Arab slogans in Jerusalem Day march
items.description: Thousands of Israeli nationalists, including young boys, join crowds chanting death threats towards Palestinians while marching through Jerusalem Old City.

items.title: How Palantir Helps Agencies 'Connect the Dots'
items.description: Palantir doesn’t "spy"—it connects siloed data so agencies can spot patterns fast.  From the CIA/FBI to major companies, the power is in the unified view. The big question: can we trust it to be used responsibly?

items.title: Cocaine hidden in imported fruit pulp worth estimated $4.6m, AFP says
items.description: Police say criminal syndicates are becoming more creative at concealing drugs within airport shipments.

items.title: 'Gut feeling': Rising Socceroos star on why he moved to Norwich City
items.description: Rising Socceroos striker Mo Toure says a "gut feeling" was the reason behind his wildly successful move to the English Championship.

items.title: Sick of maintaining your lawn? Transform it into a native garden
items.description: Many of us are looking to create a native garden as a lower maintenance, more sustainable and often cheaper alternative.

items.title: As the eldest daughter, I always knew I would care for my parents
items.description: As the eldest daughter in a Vietnamese family, it was an unspoken expectation I would be the one to care for my aging parents.

items.title: Melanie Lynskey joins the fight for justice after NZ's Pike River Mine disaster
items.description: Standing side by side with real-life heroes Anna Osborne and Sonya Rockhouse, the Yellow Jackets star is a passionate ally for their cause.

items.title: Eight people arrested at North Adelaide Golf Course redevelopment site, police say
items.description: Police say eight people have been arrested at the North Adelaide Golf Course redevelopment site this morning.

items.title: Breaking: Education union endorses deal giving Victorian teachers up to 32pc pay rise
items.description: A drawn out pay dispute between Victoria's government and public sector teachers is set to come to an end, with the union endorsing a deal for pay rises between 28 and 32 per cent.

items.title: Inquest into death of Clare Nowland hears from relatives on final day
items.description: Family of Clare Nowland have addressed a coroners court on the final day of an inquest examining her death.

items.title: Soon after John quit the Liberal Party, the strange phone calls started
items.description: When John Ternel quit the Victorian Liberal Party this week the party mistakenly sent an email to members saying he had died. Mr Ternel says the ordeal confirmed to him that the Victorian Liberals are in shambles.

items.title: Live: Oil trades higher as Trump, Xi discuss war in Iran
items.description: The ASX opened higher in morning trading after rallies on Wall Street, but was slightly down after midday. Oil is trading higher as US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discuss the war. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Surfers conquer 'terrifying' tidal rapid in remote WA
items.description: Pro surfers Anthony Walsh and Dylan Graves have conquered the never-before-surfed Talbot Bay tidal rapid in Western Australia's remote north.

items.title: National commissioner says review into Kumanjayi Little Baby won't 'cut it'
items.description: The National Commissioner for Indigenous children has criticised the selection of a retired NSW police commissioner and long-standing NT public servant as the leaders of a review into the territory's child protection system.

items.title: Matthew Wale becomes Solomon Islands prime minister after secret ballot win
items.description: Matthew Wale is the new prime minister of Solomon Islands after winning a vote in the Pacific island nation's parliament.
